ModMetaData.name: Dynamic Diplomacy Arena Fixes
ModMetaData.author: ifchen0
ModMetaData.description:
Unofficial fix for Dynamic Diplomacy - Continued.
1) Fixes this error during NPC conquest battles: System.OverflowException: Value was either too large or too small for an Int32. at DynamicDiplomacy.IncidentWorker_NPCConquest.InitArenaMap
Cause: InitArenaMap builds a raid seed with int.Parse(tickCreated.ToString() + map.uniqueID). In long-running saves the concatenated number exceeds Int32.MaxValue, so roughly 37.5% of NPC conquest battles throw before any AI is assigned. Both armies then spawn without orders and wander off the map, and the battle is resolved by auto-calc after timeout (in semi-simulation mode, the arena retries and keeps spawning more pawns).
Fix: A Harmony transpiler replaces that single int.Parse call. Values that fit in Int32 are unchanged; larger values are folded deterministically into range.
2) Better "basic AI" for arena battles In the original basic AI branch, both sides are ordered to defend the map center, which turns every fight into a melee brawl and cripples ranged / high-tech factions. With this patch: - Attacker hunts down and engages the nearest defenders (using Dynamic Diplomacy's own raid AI). - Defender holds a position near its own entry, at least 14 cells away from the map edge (same position finder the siege/shelling AI uses). Shelling AI and Factional War AI branches are unchanged. If anything fails, it falls back to the original behavior.
3) Semi-simulation battles are fought out With "simulated conquest" and "semi-simulation" both enabled in Dynamic Diplomacy, a battle site nobody enters within 2 days is no longer decided by auto-calc: the arena map is generated and the armies fight it out, as in full simulation. If that fight has not ended 2 days later and none of your pawns are on the map, auto-calc decides it. Follows Dynamic Diplomacy's own settings; no separate toggle.
4) Defeated rebel factions are cleaned up Rebellions create new factions, but defeated ones are never removed and pile up in the save. Once a day, a defeated faction that has an older faction of the same kind is removed through vanilla's own faction removal, as soon as nothing (pawns, quests, caravans, battles) still uses it. The oldest faction of each kind is always kept.
5) Optional: diplomacy changes can involve your faction Dynamic Diplomacy's diplomacy changes only ever pair two NPC factions. A new option in Dynamic Diplomacy's own settings (off by default) lets a random NPC faction make peace with you or turn hostile about as many times per year as you set. Goodwill only moves as far as needed to change the relation (peace: 0, war: -75).
6) Conquered settlements are destroyed properly When Dynamic Diplomacy conquers, razes or splits off a settlement, it only takes the old one off the map, so other mods never learn it is gone. With this patch the old settlement is destroyed the normal way, and mods clean up after it as they do for their own defeats (for example World Domination's turrets and advanced buildings, which used to stay behind). Structures left behind earlier are not removed.
7) Event frequency in times per year Dynamic Diplomacy also adds diplomacy changes (2-4 a year) and conquests (3-5 a year) to every storyteller, on top of its "extra chance" sliders, and those sliders only go down to 1% per 6 hours (2.4 a year). Its settings now show, for each event, a base count (the storyteller part, 0 turns it off), an extra count per year that can go below 1, and the total.
8) Alliance and relation fixes - With simulated conquest on, the "great alliance" step never ran. It now runs when a conquest battle starts, honouring "exclude Empire" and permanent enemies. - Rebellions and battle sites set factions hostile without changing goodwill, so the war could end silently. Goodwill now follows the relation. - If a battle site's settlement was destroyed or changed owner meanwhile, the attacker's win no longer replaces or razes it. - Battle sites were marked as belonging to your faction. They now have no faction. - Pollution on a battle site map (burst or leftover wastepacks) no longer costs goodwill with nearby factions.
9) Optional: battles on the settlement map A fourth arena style next to basic, factional war and shelling. The battle map is generated the way the contested settlement's own map would be, so the defender holds a real base with the garrison that map comes with, and the attacker comes in from the map edge with the basic AI above. - Custom Base Framework bases are used when it handles that faction, and Better Settlement Defense roles apply to the garrison. Neither is required. - The fight is decided by the garrison: civilians, turrets and later reinforcements do not count. - Chance per battle is set under the threat points in Dynamic Diplomacy's settings (default 25%, 0 turns it off). - Defenders win most of these fights. Attacker strength is left as is on purpose. - Generating a base map takes a few seconds, longer than the open field.
Notes: - Safe to add to an existing save. To remove it, do so when no NPC arena battle is in progress. - Load after Harmony and Dynamic Diplomacy - Continued. - If the original mod fixes the overflow, a warning appears in the log. - "Reached max signals per frame (3000)" when an NPC army sets up a siege camp is logged as a warning, so it no longer opens the log window in dev mode. The dropped signals only notify old quests the faction once took part in.
Dev tools: with Development mode on, Debug actions > "Dynamic Diplomacy Fix" can trigger a conquest arena with a forced AI branch (basic / factional war / shelling / settlement map / random) for quick testing, "Semi-sim: time out battle sites now / arena fights now" skip the 2-day waits, "Remove defeated duplicate factions now" runs the daily cleanup at once, and "Player diplomacy event now" triggers one player diplomacy change.
This mod was developed with the help of AI coding tools (Claude Code). Full source code is included in the Source folder for review.
